review_kind: AI-assisted factual and reader-planning scope review

source.evidence: oversees the Bear River Band Museum

practice.question: Hypothetical reader question: What would I need to decide before sharing a description of a cultural collection I am authorized to work with?
steps: Read the Band’s Tribal Historic Preservation Office page. In a private note, identify the museum and cultural program responsibilities it describes, with the source URL and check date.
Prepare a blank permissions register with fields for the custodian, proposed audience, purpose, permitted uses, attribution, access conditions and review date. Mark unanswered fields as unresolved.
For a project you are authorized to plan, identify who can approve each proposed use. Keep unanswered questions visible and arrange review before preparing material for publication.
practice.boundary: This private planning exercise draws on the Band’s public description. Communities set their own rules for cultural material. Apply those rules and the relevant permissions to any real project.
practice.reflection: Who can approve the proposed use, and how would the plan respond if a custodian limits access or requests removal?

source_limits: The Band’s page describes an undated office role. It provides no program start date or general permission to reuse material.
The permissions-register exercise is a ZOTHEOS reader proposal. No Band policy, endorsement, legal determination or service offering is inferred.
